title: danolner_dot_net
text:
About
Data scientist / geospatial analyst working on political and spatial economy research, climate and regional development, research, writing, and communication.
I work collaboratively on creative problem-solving, applying appropriate methods and technologies while considering systemic implications. Three key motivations drive my work:

Complex technical challenges—especially geography-related ones
Contributing to thriving regions and a stable, zero-carbon biosphere
Writing as a thinking tool


“The point is to raise up our humanity. Imagination and hope will be our twin guides.” — Roberto Unger

title: danolner_dot_net
text:
Writing
Writing is crystallised life. I’ve authored:

A near-future sci-fi novel titled The Ink that Draws the Maps
A short story available for download
Various academic, technical, and reflective posts

I participate in Sheffield’s Writers’ Workshop and credit writing communities as essential to my work.

title: danolner_dot_net
text:
Projects

Regional Economic Analysis (South Yorkshire)

Role with Y-PERN and SYMCA on growth and skills strategy. Created sector analysis and data accessibility tools, developed open code and data resources for ONS business demography, and organized policy forums connecting researchers and policymakers. Focus: “strengthening the glue” between university research and regional policy.


Spatial Economy & Zero Carbon Transition

Re-wiring the spatial economy for zero carbon
Built models of UK internal trade flow scenarios. Found that spatial economics and distance still matter despite transition challenges.
Technologies: Stata, R, ArcGIS
Publication: “The spatial economics of energy justice” (Energy Policy, 2020)


Wind Farms & Property Values (Scotland)

Project with ClimateXChange Scotland. Built line-of-sight framework accounting for building heights and landscape. Result: didn’t find statistical evidence of price effects. Visualization showed green space visibility patterns in Glasgow.


A Tale of Two Countries

Interactive data story tool examining English inequality (2015-2019). Uses Index of Multiple Deprivation data.
Technologies: D3, JavaScript, R


Harmonised UK Census Data (1971-2011)

Created consistent geographies across five decades. Used in research on immigration’s local employment impacts. Published research became the journal’s “most downloaded article ever”.


Systems not Lightbulbs

Guide for building zero-carbon pathways in higher education. Co-written with Sheffield Carbon Neutral University team. Includes case studies and movement-building strategies. Illustrations by Eliot Robinson.


3D Geographical Data Prints

Physical visualizations of Census and other spatial variables. Uses include public engagement and accessibility for blind users. Example: violent crime mapping in Rotherham.


Social Frontiers in Rotterdam

Collaboration with TU Delft examining neighborhood demographics. Analysis of household mobility patterns across social boundaries.
Publication: “The conflicting geographies of social frontiers” (Environment & Planning B, 2023)


House Price Network Visualization (Glasgow)

Examined spatial correlation of price movements. Revealed underlying market area patterns separated by geographic features.
Technologies: Java/Processing, R


PhD Research

Topic: Agent-based modeling approach to spatial economic theory
Addressed gap in quantitative tools for spatial economic change assessment. Created interactive Java framework for economic modeling. Produced novel models replicating established economic patterns (Alonso-Muth-Mills, Krugman core-periphery). Explored economic history and self-organized systems.

Writing Topics & Archive

Economic & Systems Theory

Adaptive landscapes and human organization systems
Stafford Beer’s Cybersyn and economic design
Economic reform vs. revolution debates
Pareto optimality and welfare comparisons
Price system emergence and self-organization



Geography & Spatial Economics

Cars’ role in urban form transformation
Containerization’s impact on port cities
Value density in logistics and spatial economics
Internet monopoly parallels to physical space



Methods & Visualization

Differences between data visualization types (boxplots vs. x-rays)
Visualization for comprehension vs. communication
Statistical methods and their explanatory limits



Climate & Environment

Climate change’s ideological entanglement
Crop genetic modification and public research
Zero-carbon transition challenges



Philosophy & Emergence

Language as pheromone trail vs. logic machine
Intention in emergent systems
“Cargo cult” thinking in systems design
Productive stupidity in research



Food Systems & Global Justice

Pharmaceutical production and open-source models
Workers in supply chains
Seed production and agricultural control
